idiom_name: builder object with step methods and a terminal build(), optionally driven by a director
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the product a private constructor and let a separate builder type carry one step method per optional setting plus the required values, each step returning the builder so calls can be chained; a terminal build() copies the accumulated state, validates the invariants of the whole object once and returns a value the caller cannot mutate further. When one sequence is needed in several places, move it into a director that takes any builder and runs the steps in order, which is what lets a single construction process produce different representations. Keep the builder out of the product's essential API: callers that do not need stepwise construction should get a plain constructor, named constructor or default, and reserve the builder for the multi-optional case.
code_sketch:
b = Product.builder(required_1, required_2)
b.timeout(5s)
b.add_header("Accept", "application/json")   # optional steps
p = b.build()                                # validates + freezes
# director: d.construct_standard(b) runs a fixed sequence over any builder
pitfalls: Wrong move: let build() store the builder's mutable collections in the product -> later builder reuse changes an already published value -> instead copy and defensively freeze every collection at the build boundary.

Wrong move: treat fluent setters as validation -> a missing required value or cross-field conflict survives until a later consumer fails -> instead require mandatory state in the builder constructor or staged types and validate the complete snapshot in build().

Wrong move: share one mutable builder across threads or branches -> interleaved calls mix configurations and make results nondeterministic -> instead use a fresh single-use builder or an explicit immutable/copy-on-write branch.

Wrong move: use a builder as a stand-in for named parameters on any object with a handful of fields -> you duplicate the product's API, lose compile-time completeness checks and every field rename touches two types -> instead simplify the class first (parameter objects, records, named arguments) and keep builders for staged, validated or multi-representation construction.

Wrong move: assume build() consumes or freezes the builder -> later calls on the still-mutable builder silently produce a second, different product -> instead enforce single use by convention, or document build() as repeatable the way java.net.http.HttpRequest.Builder does by returning a new immutable request per call.

Wrong move: route every test's construction through one production builder and rely on its defaults -> builder refactors break unrelated tests and hidden defaults conceal what each test asserts -> instead keep test data builders separate from production builders and have tests pass every value they assert.
